note: Parent Arabic Guide (Screen 16). Today's tip = tips[dayOfYear % tips.length]. Optional per tip: girl_label/girl_ar/girl_say, reply_ar/reply_say. audio:true = show the listen button (only fully vowelled phrases).

tips.title: Short vowels
tips.rule: Three small marks give short vowel sounds. Fatha (ـَ) above = short 'a'. Kasra (ـِ) below = short 'i' as in 'sit'. Damma (ـُ) above = short 'u' as in 'put'.

tips.title: Long vowels
tips.rule: To stretch a vowel, add a letter: ا makes a long 'aa', ي makes a long 'ee', و makes a long 'oo'.

tips.title: Sukun = no vowel
tips.rule: A small circle (ـْ) above a letter means it has no vowel. You just say the consonant and stop.

tips.title: Shadda = double letter
tips.rule: A small 'w' shape (ـّ) means say the letter twice, holding it a little longer.

tips.title: Dots change the letter
tips.rule: Many letters share one shape and differ only by dots. Count the dots and check if they are above or below.

tips.title: Right to left
tips.rule: Arabic is read and written from right to left. Point your finger at the right side of the line to start.

tips.title: Letters change shape
tips.rule: Most letters look different at the start, middle and end of a word. It is still the same letter.

tips.title: Letters that don't join forward
tips.rule: Six letters never connect to the letter after them: ا د ذ ر ز و. That's why some words have small gaps inside.

tips.title: Sounds with no English match
tips.rule: ع ح خ غ ق come from the throat. Don't worry about perfection; let your child copy the app audio.

tips.title: Heavy and light pairs
tips.rule: Some pairs sound close, but the second one is 'heavier' (deeper in the mouth): س/ص, ت/ط, د/ض, ذ/ظ.

tips.title: Hamza = a tiny stop
tips.rule: Hamza (ء) is a short catch in the throat, like the break in 'uh-oh'.

tips.title: 'The' = ال
tips.rule: Arabic has no separate word for 'the'. Attach ال (al-) to the front of the word.

tips.title: 'A / an' is hidden
tips.rule: There is no word for 'a'. The 'n' sound at the end (tanween, ـٌ ـً ـٍ) does the job.

tips.title: Moon letters
tips.rule: With moon letters you hear the 'l' in ال clearly.

tips.title: Sun letters
tips.rule: With sun letters (like ت د ر س ش ن) the 'l' is silent and the next letter is doubled instead.

tips.title: Masculine and feminine
tips.rule: Every noun is masculine or feminine. A ة at the end usually means feminine.

tips.title: ة or ه?
tips.rule: ة (with 2 dots) only appears at the end of a word and sounds like 'a'. ه has no dots and sounds like 'h'.

tips.title: Adjectives come after
tips.rule: The describing word comes after the noun, the opposite of English.

tips.title: Adjectives match gender
tips.rule: If the noun is feminine, add ة to the adjective too.
tips.example_en: a big house  a big car

tips.title: Colours change for feminine
tips.rule: Colours have their own feminine form, not just ة.

tips.title: No 'is' in simple sentences
tips.rule: In present-tense sentences Arabic skips 'is' and 'are'.

tips.title: 'The big house' vs 'The house is big'
tips.rule: If both words have ال it's a phrase. If only the noun has ال, it's a sentence.
tips.example_en: the big house  the house is big

tips.title: This: هذا / هذه
tips.rule: Use هذا for masculine nouns and هذه for feminine nouns.
tips.example_en: this is a chair  this is a table

tips.title: That: ذلك / تلك
tips.rule: For something far away, use ذلك (masculine) or تلك (feminine).
tips.example_en: that is a house  that is a car

tips.title: What is this?
tips.rule: ما هذا؟ asks about a thing. Answer with هذا + the word.
tips.example_en: What is this? This is a pen

tips.title: Who is this?
tips.rule: مَن asks about a person.
tips.example_en: Who is this? This is my dad

tips.title: Where?
tips.rule: أين asks where something is. في = in, على = on.
tips.example_en: Where is the cat? The cat is on the chair

tips.title: Yes/no questions
tips.rule: Put هل at the start to make a yes/no question. Answer with نعم (yes) or لا (no).

tips.title: I, you, he, she
tips.rule: 'You' changes for a boy or a girl.

tips.title: 'My' is an ending
tips.rule: Add ـي to the end of a word to say 'my'.

tips.title: 'Your' and 'his' are endings too
tips.rule: Add ـكَ for 'your' (boy), ـكِ for 'your' (girl), and ـه for 'his'.

tips.title: 'And' sticks to the next word
tips.rule: و (and) is written with no space before the next word.

tips.title: Two of something
tips.rule: Arabic has a special 'two' form: add ـان to the end.

tips.title: Easy plurals
tips.rule: Many feminine words make a plural by swapping ة for ـات.

tips.title: Broken plurals
tips.rule: Many plurals change the inside of the word. These are learned one by one, so don't worry about rules.

tips.title: Arabic numbers
tips.rule: Textbooks use these digits, and they are written left to right even inside Arabic text.

tips.title: Vowel marks disappear later
tips.rule: Kids' books show every vowel mark. Adult texts usually drop them, so readers rely on knowing the word.

tips.title: School Arabic vs home Arabic
tips.rule: School uses Fusha (standard Arabic). Words at home may differ, so both are fine; just know the textbook form for homework.

tips.title: Everyday greeting
tips.rule: The standard greeting and its reply are great for daily practice at the door.
tips.example_en: Peace be upon you  and upon you peace

tips.title: Thank you / you're welcome
tips.rule: Use these at home every day to build the habit.

tips.title: What is this?
tips.rule: Point at anything and ask. For a feminine thing, use هذه instead.

tips.title: Where is…?
tips.rule: Hide a toy and ask. Swap in any word your child knows.

tips.title: Look here!
tips.rule: Great for showing your child something. The ending changes for a girl.

tips.title: Let's play!
tips.rule: Use it to start any game, and get your child to say it to siblings.

tips.title: It's my turn
tips.rule: Perfect for board games and taking turns.

tips.title: Come with me
tips.rule: Say it when you walk somewhere together.

tips.title: I won!
tips.rule: Let your child shout it after a game.

tips.title: I'm hungry
tips.rule: Ask your child to say it before snacks.

tips.title: I want water
tips.rule: Practise it at every meal.

tips.title: Please
tips.rule: Add it to any request. The ending depends on who you ask.

tips.title: Help me
tips.rule: Encourage your child to ask for help in Arabic.

tips.title: I finished
tips.rule: Say it after homework, meals or tidying up.

tips.title: Good morning
tips.rule: Start every day with it. The reply means 'morning of light'.

tips.title: Good night
tips.rule: Make it your bedtime routine. It changes when said to a girl.

tips.title: I love you
tips.rule: Say it every day. It changes for a girl.
